brief: Rail: every line's path, colors, shared track, line letters, line ends and end signs, stations and their marks at every zoom.
Buses: bus lines and frequency tiers, shared streets, arrows on one-way stretches, terminals, route numbers, part-time service.
Names: station, street, town and route labels. Collisions, labels far from what they name, missing names, names that change or jump between zooms.
Dark mode: the same views in the dark theme. Contrast, marks that lose their edge, basemap features that glare or vanish, the Key and panels in dark.

Tapping things: route, station, stop, Park-n-Ride and FlexRide panels, search, the Lines list, the Key, Back closing what is open, the installed web app. Wrong or missing information, dead ends, panels covering what they describe.
Access: keyboard path to everything, focus order and visibility, screen-reader names and announcements, text size and zoom, touch target sizes. axe-core is a start, not the whole check.
Speed: load on a throttled slow-4G phone profile. Time to rail, data and script sizes, anything fetched twice or too early, jank while panning.

Matches RTD's data: compare what is drawn with GTFS and RTD's ArcGIS layers. Routes drawn where GTFS says they run, frequency tiers that match the schedule, stops where GTFS puts them, service days, station service, anything RTD has that the map lacks.
Does what DESIGN.md promises: take the one DESIGN.md section least recently audited (ledger spec_sections) and check every claim in it against the running site and the code.

Precedents: compare with the maps DESIGN.md cites (MTA Live Subway Map, Transit app maps, LOOM output, RTD's own system map). Find one thing they do clearly better that this map could adopt, or a mistake they avoid that this map makes.
